Careening down the cobbled hill street, a buttercup-yellow sledge sends a rooster-tail of powder off its left runner, the tiny painted sledder leaning hard into the curve, a toppled milk churn spinning in the wake behind, its flanks and panels one plain block of painted colour wearing a single small painted picture.

Swinging out over ink-dark water, the lighthouse beam catches the spray mid-air, thousands of lit droplets hanging in it, the painted keeper a grain-of-rice silhouette in the lamp-room doorway, the rocks below still silvered where the light has just passed.

Bursting off the snow-buried rooftop in a copper-and-charcoal explosion, forty painted starlings scatter upward, the lowest birds still in tight formation, the highest already breaking apart like thrown pepper against the violet sky.

Leaning back on the hempen rope with the great verdigris bell already tipped well past its balance point, a tiny painted bellringer plants both heels on the flagstone, the rope's arc still curved above the empty belfry.

Skidding on black ice with one scarlet-booted foot stamped hard to the ground, a painted postie fights the handlebars of a holly-green bicycle, the canvas satchel swinging wide, three envelopes mid-tumble from its open flap, its flanks and panels one plain block of painted colour wearing a single small painted picture.

Winding up the lantern-lit hill with the front of the procession already curling round the granite bend, a straggling file of painted carol singers clutches crimson candles, the last two figures still stepping off the cobbled square below.

Halfway up a soot-blackened ladder propped against a honey-brick chimney, a painted sweep in a peacock-teal coat reaches for the next rung, the dropped brush spinning handle-first toward the snow three storeys beneath.

Tilting into a hard left turn on the hill road, a lacquered scarlet sleigh kicks twin arcs of ice-crystal off its gilded runners, the tiny painted driver hauling the reins, the horses' hoof-prints still scored in a long curve behind, its flanks and panels one plain block of painted colour wearing a single small painted picture.

Half-inflated and straining against its rope tethers, a tangerine balloon envelope billows into the pewter sky, two painted balloonists in indigo coats hauling the burner chain, the wicker basket still tilted sideways on the frozen grass, its flanks and panels one plain block of painted colour wearing a single small painted picture.

Cresting the amber dune with the caravan's carved roof catching the last copper light, a painted driver in a saffron headscarf urges two tiny painted horses forward, the deep wheel-ruts still fresh and dark in the sand below, its flanks and panels one plain block of painted colour wearing a single small painted picture.

Mid-stride on the oval pond with a long curved silver scratch stretching behind his blade, a painted skater in a claret coat leans into the next stroke, arms wide, a dropped amber scarf still uncoiling on the ice behind him.

Lifting off a warm terracotta chimney on wings the colour of old bronze, a dragon the size of a painted cat arches its back mid-launch, three loose roof-tiles rocking in its wake, one still balanced at the chimney's lip.

Punching through the near tunnel-mouth with its amber windows blazing against the soot-black brickwork, a painted train trails a white steam plume that hangs in a long curve back across the viaduct it has just crossed, its flanks and panels one plain block of painted colour wearing a single small painted picture.

Spinning with one gilded car cresting the apex, a painted ferris wheel catches the last rose light on its spokes, the tiny painted rider in the high car leaning out, a dropped cobalt scarf still falling toward the fairground below.

Mid-spin, a carousel of crimson horses blurs past the painted ticket booth, one tiny painted rider leaning forward with arm outstretched, fingertips nearly brushing the brass ring swinging on its post at the edge of the platform.

Propping the bottle-green shutter open with a wide timber tray still steaming in one hand, a painted baker in a flour-white apron wedges a boot against the sill, three golden loaves tilting on the tray's far corner.

Caught in the air six inches above the painted retriever's nose, a pine-green stick tumbles end over end, the tiny painted dog mid-leap beneath it, paws off the snow, its own footprints ending abruptly at the launch point.

Whipping off the line in a gust, a sheet of ox-blood red cloth snaps horizontal above the rooftop, two wooden pegs already bouncing down the tiles, the remaining washing still pinned and flailing in the same hard wind.

Banging against the stone wall on its iron hinge, a cobalt shutter swings fully open in mid-gust, the latch dangling free, a painted pot of dried herbs on the sill inside teetering at the edge it has clearly just slid to.

Arriving through the harbour gap with its rust-orange hull trailing a white V-wake still spreading across the grey water, a painted fishing boat leans slightly to starboard, the tiny painted deckhand already coiling a rope at the bow, its flanks and panels one plain block of painted colour wearing a single small painted picture.

Frozen mid-tumble at the bottom of the toboggan run in a tangle of lime-green and violet sleds, three painted figures sprawl in the churned snow, one sled still spinning on its side, a knitted hat pinwheeling in the cold air above, its flanks and panels one plain block of painted colour wearing a single small painted picture.

Hanging a tin lantern on the outermost branch of a snow-laden fir, a tiny painted figure in a vermillion coat stretches on tiptoe, the lit lantern already swinging, a warm amber circle spreading on the snow below.

Half-swung across the lane with its candy-stripe boom still moving, a level-crossing gate catches a painted stationmaster mid-crank, the tiny handle still turning, the gate's far end still two feet short of the post it is aiming for.

Pushed off the ice with a long pole, a butter-yellow rowboat tilts at the moment of launch, a painted deckhand in a jade coat leaning on the pole, the dark water already opening in a thin line behind the hull, its flanks and panels one plain block of painted colour wearing a single small painted picture.

Thrown from a painted carol singer's mitten and caught in perfect stillness three inches from the nose of a laughing painted figure across the ring, a dense white snowball hangs in the lamplight, its shadow already on the cobblestones below.
